question: After companion-side final revalidation is added, should OpenClaw adopt deny-over-allow policy in both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json as a supported core security contract?
rationale: The implementation adds persistent config and protocol surface and intentionally changes security=full with ask=off, so product and security ownership cannot be inferred from code correctness alone.

options.title: Adopt after boundary fix
options.body: Accept the feature once gateway, node-local, and macOS companion execution enforce the same final denylist-revocation contract.

options.title: Limit to approvals file
options.body: Keep the feature under the existing exec-approvals policy owner and remove the new openclaw.json surface.

options.title: Decline the core feature
options.body: Do not establish deny-by-exception as a supported core execution-policy contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt after boundary fix
recommendation.body: Accept the feature once gateway, node-local, and macOS companion execution enforce the same final denylist-revocation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects steipete directly to the macOS companion authorization and revoked-forwarded-approval contract that owns this decision.
